title: tenant-claim-hashing-kms-origin-gate-and-rbac-lattice
author: Sofia Martinez
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers operating across multiple regions asked for a deterministic, privacy-preserving tenant proof token that can travel in request headers for routing, KMS origin verification, and end-to-end audit correlation. Existing ephemeral attestation approaches were brittle across proxies and caused noisy audit streams when a service re-signed payloads.

What this PR does: Introduces a tenant-claim tokenizer that deterministically derives a short proof token from a tenant's stable claims (tenant_id, account_zone, service_role) using a configurable hashing + HMAC envelope. Adds KMS origin gating to the KMS allocator: the allocator now validates that a requested key usage includes an origin fingerprint that matches the signing key's allowed origins; mismatches produce a clear audit event and are rejected. Adds an RBAC v2 "lattice translator" that turns claim-based grant entries into lattice rules the runtime enforcer consumes; this provides an auditable mapping and a point-in-time migration path for older role bindings. Wires a new signed-audit-token header into the API middleware so downstream services and audit collectors can reliably correlate requests without leaking raw tenant claims.

Implementation highlights: - services/audit/tokenizer: deterministic claim hashing, HMAC envelope, short token encoding (base62) and optional ephemeral key signing. Token format versioning is built-in. - infra/kms/origin_gate.go: origin fingerprinting, allowlist checks, clean audit rejection path and metrics (kms.origin.rejects, kms.origin.latency). - pkg/rbac/lattice/transformer.go: rule translator with migration flag to produce both legacy bindings and lattice rules during rollout. - audit pipeline (pkg/audit/receiver): parser for signed-audit-token, correlation id extraction and dedupe hints for stream consumer. - tests: unit tests for tokenizer edge cases, allocator gating tests, and an e2e test exercising cross-region routing against a mocked KMS.

Checklist (completed): - [x] Add deterministic tokenizer service and API docs. - [x] Enforce KMS origin gate in allocator and add metrics. - [x] Implement RBAC v2 lattice translator and unit tests. - [x] Wire signed-audit-token into middleware and audit receiver. - [x] Integration tests for common failure modes and migration path. - [x] Docs and rollout plan for enterprise customers.

Rollout plan: staged rollout using a feature flag: "tenant_proof_tokens". Phase 1 (internal): enable for 10% of traffic with translator in read-only migration mode to collect mapping telemetry. Phase 2: increase to 50% and enable allocator gating for non-critical tenants. Phase 3: 100% with full enforcement and deprecation of legacy attestation header. Backout: feature flag off; allocator rejects are converted into soft-audit events when safe.

Risks and mitigations: - Risk: token format change could break downstream consumers. Mitigation: token includes version prefix and tokenizer package provides compatibility helpers. - Risk: false rejections in KMS allocator. Mitigation: start in logging mode; provide diagnostic endpoint to replay failed allocations.

Notes: this PR focuses on enforcement and mapping; a follow-up will add an admin UI in Console for token decoding and a migration dashboard that surfaces translation mismatches.

release_notes:
- Introduced deterministic tenant-proof tokens (short, hashed, versioned) for routing and audit correlation.
- KMS allocator now enforces origin gating and emits kms.origin.reject metrics when mismatches occur.
- RBAC v2 lattice translator for claim-based grant migration; allows staged migration to the lattice enforcer.
- Signed-audit-token header added to the middleware and audit pipeline to improve provenance tracking.
